canonical.title: Multi-monitor, window management and the desktop shell: replacing DisplayFusion, Fences, FancyZones and X-Rite on Linux

parent.title: Throwing away Windows: a replacement plan for an actual installed-software inventory

siblings.title: Your .NET + SQL Server stack on Linux: what actually replaces what
siblings.summary: Rider replaces Visual Studio + ReSharper on Linux at the cost of the WinForms/WPF designers; SQL Server itself moves cleanly to a container, but SSMS has no Linux successor now that Azure Data Studio is dead.

siblings.title: Microsoft 365 on Linux in 2026: what you actually lose
siblings.summary: Office, Teams and mail are a tolerable compromise on Linux in 2026; OneDrive sync and OneNote are the two places where the gap is real.

siblings.title: The utility belt: per-tool Linux verdicts for a Windows power user (2026)
siblings.summary: Per-tool verdicts for the Windows-only utilities in an actual installed-software inventory: most transfer cleanly, AutoHotkey and Power Automate Desktop have no single answer, and Wayland is the variable that decides the rest.

siblings.title: Gaming after the switch: your library survives, the NVIDIA App does not
siblings.summary: Both installed games run under Proton — Planetfall is Gold/Deck-Playable and Fall Guys' EAC is Linux-enabled — so the only hard loss is the NVIDIA App and Game Bar tooling layer, which becomes environment variables plus MangoHud and GPU Screen Recorder.

siblings.title: Legion hardware, peripherals and the two corporate VPNs on Linux
siblings.summary: Neither corporate VPN blocks the switch — Harmony SASE ships an official Linux agent and WatchGuard is reachable with plain OpenVPN; the real losses are QuantumENGINE, Dolby, XTU and Lenovo's AI/Space bloat.

siblings.title: Escape hatches for the leftovers: Wine, a VM, passthrough, or just keep the partition
siblings.summary: Wine for single-window utilities, a local Windows VM for Visual Studio and SSMS, RDP for the corporate cluster — and no GPU passthrough on a muxless Legion.

sources.title: KDE Plasma 6.7 announcement
sources.claim: Plasma 6.7 shipped per-screen virtual desktops after 21 years and allows an ICC profile while HDR is active.

sources.title: OMG! Ubuntu — KDE Plasma 6.7 released
sources.claim: Each connected monitor in Plasma 6.7 can show a separate virtual desktop; released June 2026.

sources.title: PlasmaZones
sources.claim: PlasmaZones is a FancyZones-style KWin zone tiler with 26 built-in layouts and per-monitor/per-desktop layouts, Wayland-only on Plasma 6.

sources.title: David Edmundson — the last X11 session
sources.claim: Plasma 6.7 is the last release that includes an X11 session.

sources.title: 9to5Linux — Plasma 6.8 goes Wayland-only
sources.claim: Plasma 6.8 (October 2026) drops the X11 session and goes Wayland-only.

sources.title: Phoronix — 95% of Plasma 6.6 users on Wayland
sources.claim: More than 95% of Plasma 6.6 users already run the Wayland session.

sources.title: DisplayFusion features
sources.claim: DisplayFusion's feature set includes multi-monitor taskbars, monitor splitting, window position profiles, per-monitor wallpaper, monitor configuration profiles, hotkeys, TitleBar buttons and Triggers.

sources.title: Stardock Fences
sources.claim: Fences 6 provides shaded icon groups, automation rules, roll-up mini-windows, Folder Portals and Peek.

sources.title: Wikipedia — Fences (software)
sources.claim: Fences organises desktop icons into moveable groups and can hide icons when not in use.

sources.title: X-Rite Color Assistant
sources.claim: X-Rite Color Assistant restores Lenovo factory-calibrated ICC profiles (sRGB, HDR, Rec.709) on ThinkPad/Legion panels.

sources.title: XDA — KDE's tiling editor vs FancyZones
sources.claim: KDE's built-in tiling layout editor works like FancyZones but cannot store or swap multiple custom layouts.

sources.title: Tiling Shell
sources.claim: Tiling Shell brings FancyZones-style layouts, a layout editor and multi-monitor support with differing scale factors to GNOME Shell 42-49.

sources.title: GNOME Extensions — Tiling Shell
sources.claim: Tiling Shell 17.3 lists GNOME Shell 50 among supported versions.

sources.title: KDE Discuss — show only tasks from current screen
sources.claim: Plasma's per-screen task filter exists but stops being honoured after resume from suspend on NVIDIA, requiring a plasmashell restart.

sources.title: Dash to Panel
sources.claim: Dash to Panel adds a Windows-style taskbar to GNOME with options to isolate running apps by workspace and/or monitor.

sources.title: KDE Discuss — single wallpaper across all displays
sources.claim: Plasma assigns wallpaper individually per screen; spanning one image across displays is an open request.

sources.title: GNOME Discourse — per-screen wallpaper request
sources.claim: GNOME still does not support a different wallpaper per screen in 2026; workarounds are manual image compositing or unmaintained extensions.

sources.title: Superpaper
sources.claim: Superpaper is a multi-monitor wallpaper manager for Linux and Windows, with a desktop-environment list rooted in X11-era tooling.

sources.title: hyprpaper (Hyprland wiki)
sources.claim: hyprpaper sets wallpapers per monitor by output name in hyprpaper.conf.

sources.title: KDE docs — Folder View
sources.claim: Plasma allows unlimited Folder View widgets on the desktop, each showing a different folder, filterable by regex or file type.

sources.title: Desktop Icons NG (rastersoft)
sources.claim: Desktop Icons NG supports 'stacking' desktop files, grouping files of the same type, since version 34.

sources.title: GNOME Extensions — Desktop Icons NG (DING)
sources.claim: Desktop Icons NG (DING) is the maintained GNOME extension providing desktop icons.

sources.title: OMG! Ubuntu — DING GTK4 port
sources.claim: DING completed its GTK4 port in v51.0.0, released July 2026, with early GNOME 51 support.

sources.title: Arch BBS — ordering icons in Folder View
sources.claim: Users report there is no way to manually order icons inside a KDE Folder View widget.

sources.title: This Week in Plasma — session restore
sources.claim: KWin implements the Wayland session management protocol in Plasma 6.7; toolkit and app adoption is the remaining gate.

sources.title: Phoronix — wayland-protocols 1.48
sources.claim: XDG Session Management shipped in wayland-protocols 1.48 on 1 April 2026 and lets clients restore window positions and state.

sources.title: RememberWindowPositions
sources.claim: The RememberWindowPositions KWin script restores window position, size, screen and virtual desktop on Plasma 6+ under both Wayland and X11, with caption-matching and session-restore caveats.

sources.title: KDE Bug 161325
sources.claim: The canonical KDE bug about losing window positions when an external monitor is temporarily unplugged is closed as a duplicate of a fixed bug.

sources.title: Arch Wiki — Kanshi
sources.claim: kanshi enables output profiles automatically on hotplug and is the Wayland equivalent of autorandr; it can blank the laptop panel when docked.

sources.title: kscreen-doctor man page
sources.claim: kscreen-doctor scripts KDE display settings by connector name, and KScreen stores configuration as JSON in ~/.config/kscreen/.

sources.title: DisplayCAL
sources.claim: DisplayCAL, powered by ArgyllCMS, supports X-Rite/Calibrite i1 Display colorimeters and can import vendor colorimeter corrections.

sources.title: displaycal-py3
sources.claim: displaycal-py3 is the maintained Python 3 fork of DisplayCAL, targeting Python 3.9+.

sources.title: Arne Baeyens — Linux display calibration (2026)
sources.claim: A 2026 Linux calibration walkthrough shows the ArgyllCMS/DisplayCAL loop and warns that applying an ICC profile only inside a colour-managed app does not set the VCGT tables.

sources.title: DisplayCAL forums — baking VCGT into a profile
sources.claim: KDE Plasma on Wayland does not support the API to set VCGT, so calibration curves must be carried in the ICC profile and applied by the CMS instead of the GPU LUT.

sources.title: Phoronix — KDE Wayland colour management
sources.claim: KDE Plasma Wayland gained per-screen colour management, so ICC profiles assigned to each screen work correctly.

sources.title: This Week in Plasma — ICC profiles + HDR
sources.claim: Plasma 6.7 allows using an ICC profile while HDR mode is active.

sources.title: Phoronix — color-management-v1 merged
sources.claim: Wayland's color-management-v1 protocol, covering ICC profiles and HDR, was merged upstream in February 2025 after five years.

sources.title: GNOME 50 release notes
sources.claim: GNOME 50, released 18 March 2026, added wp_color_management version 2, HDR screen sharing, fractional scaling, VRR and NVIDIA driver-quirk workarounds.

sources.title: botmonster — mixed-DPI multi-monitor Linux
sources.claim: In 2026 every major compositor does per-monitor fractional scaling; KDE allows arbitrary scale values while GNOME is limited to 25% steps, and XWayland apps are rescaled and appear soft with a 5-10% GPU cost.

sources.title: AlternativeTo — Plasma 6.3 fractional scaling and panel cloning
sources.claim: Plasma 6.3 reworked fractional scaling for pixel-grid alignment, added panel cloning, and improved colour accuracy with or without ICC profiles.

sources.title: falcao.org — NVIDIA on Fedora KDE Wayland (May 2026)
sources.claim: A May 2026 field report on NVIDIA 595.71.05 with Plasma 6.6 finds explicit sync removed a class of NVIDIA-specific Wayland glitches, multi-monitor with mixed refresh rates works, VRR may need kscreen-doctor, and open kernel modules are the only option on Blackwell.

sources.title: UbuntuHandbook — NVIDIA 595.58.03
sources.claim: NVIDIA 595.58.03 (March 2026) enables nvidia-drm.ko modeset=1 by default and adds DRI3 1.2 with DMA fences.

sources.title: 9to5Linux — NVIDIA 595 requires Wayland 1.20
sources.claim: The NVIDIA 595 branch raises the minimum supported Wayland version to 1.20.

sources.title: open-gpu-kernel-modules issue 161
sources.claim: GNOME/mutter fails to initialise the NVIDIA dGPU and falls back to CPU rendering when a secondary screen is attached directly to it in hybrid setups; single-display hybrid works.

sources.title: NVIDIA forums — external monitor on hybrid laptops
sources.claim: External monitors on hybrid NVIDIA+Intel laptops under Wayland are reported as unusable across GNOME, KDE Plasma and Cinnamon.

sources.title: NVIDIA forums — blank external outputs in hybrid mode
sources.claim: On Lenovo Legion laptops all external outputs (USB-C and HDMI) are wired to the NVIDIA GPU only, and hybrid graphics mode yields a blank external display.

sources.title: Arch BBS — Legion Hybrid (iGPU only) mode
sources.claim: Lenovo Legion 'Hybrid (iGPU only)' BIOS graphics mode causes its own problems on Linux.

sources.title: Arch Wiki — Variable refresh rate
sources.claim: KWin's Wayland session automatically enables VRR for fullscreen applications, and unlike X11 multiple monitors do not break G-Sync/FreeSync.

sources.title: niri
sources.claim: niri treats multi-monitor as core to its design with working mixed DPI and pixel-perfect fractional scaling, and documents no colour management/HDR.

sources.title: kanshi
sources.claim: kanshi defines output profiles enabled and disabled automatically on hotplug for compositors supporting wlr-output-management.

sources.title: GNOME Shell dev blog — multi-monitor workspaces
sources.claim: GNOME Shell offers only two multi-monitor workspace modes: workspaces spanning all displays, or workspaces on the primary display only.

sources.title: GNOME Discourse — independent workspaces per monitor
sources.claim: Independent per-monitor workspaces remain an open feature request in GNOME, not a shipped capability.
